hints: Focus on the definition of bond energy as the enthalpy needed to break a covalent bond to form separate gaseous atoms.
Notice that one $\text{CH}_4$ molecule contains four identical C-H bonds, so to get just one mole of C-H bonds you need only one quarter of a mole of methane.
Remember breaking bonds is endothermic, so the gaseous atoms must appear on the product side for a positive bond energy value.
walkthrough:
**Recall what average bond energy means**

Think of it simply as the energy needed to snap one mole of a particular bond in the gas phase.

The rule is: gaseous molecule $\rightarrow$ separate gaseous atoms, breaking exactly $1$ mol of that bond:
$$\text{E(C-H)} = \Delta H \text{ for breaking 1 mol C-H(g)}$$

**Count how many C-H bonds are in methane**

Methane has four C-H bonds per molecule, so full atomisation breaks four moles of C-H:
$$\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{C(g)} + 4\text{H(g)}$$

**Scale down to one mole of bonds**

To get the average per single C-H bond, divide the whole atomisation equation by 4.

That gives one mole of C-H broken to give gaseous atoms:
$$\tfrac{1}{4}\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} \rightarrow \tfrac{1}{4}\text{C(g)} + \text{H(g)}$$

**Check direction and states**

Bond breaking must be written as decomposition to atoms, not formation from atoms, and all species must be gaseous. This matches the scaled equation exactly, so that is the average bond energy.

options.A: This shows bond making, $\tfrac{1}{4}\text{C(g)} + \text{H(g)} \rightarrow \tfrac{1}{4}\text{CH}_4\text{(g)}$. Forming bonds releases energy, so its enthalpy change is the negative of the bond energy, not the bond energy itself.
options.B: This shows exactly one mole of C-H bonds broken in the gas phase to give separate gaseous atoms. Starting from $\tfrac{1}{4}$ mol of $\text{CH}_4$ means $1$ mol of C-H is broken, which is precisely the definition of average bond energy.
options.C: This shows $\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{C(g)} + 4\text{H(g)}$. It breaks four moles of C-H bonds, so its enthalpy is four times the average bond energy. It is the total atomisation enthalpy of methane, not the average per bond.
options.D: This shows $\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{(g)} + \text{H(g)}$. It breaks only the first C-H bond to give a methyl radical. That is the first bond dissociation energy, which is different from the average over all four bonds.
